Fred Clay has lent valuable assistance, as have Bert Machell and Alan Fleming. This is another event in which we shall have to unearth some new talent.

Unfortunately Alan Fleming, our best Junior here, has joined the R.A.F. and has been unable to turn out at all for us. The first post-war Club Championships were very well supported and from the results to be found on another page, it will be seen that not one of the 1939 winners retained his title.
Included on the same programme were two Club Junior Handicaps, and with two heats in the 220 Yards the following qualified for the final : Sexton, A.

We were glad to see Alan Fleming turn out in the Long Jump Championship and gain second place with 19 feet 7½ inches. This was not so good as he had been doing in R.A.F. events, but we hope he will be able to reproduce that form when he returns to civilian life.
